name: store-en
title: English Chrome Web Store screenshot series (v6 — dictionary)
style: v6 — v5 unchanged in palette and geometry; what changes is WHAT the series shows. The word lookup shipped in 1.0.21 (hover card, word screen, the standing saved mark) and none of it was in the v5 captures, so slide 2 was re-shot against it and slide 5 added.
sourceOfTruth: slide1..5.html — English copy is inline in the HTML

captures.recapture: node apps/youtube/screenshots/capture-backdrop.mjs --locale en --learn es --native en --modes sidebar,guess,settings --class vtt-light
captures.note: Shared by every pipeline (~345 MB, 2560x1600 PNG) and therefore referenced, not vendored. render.mjs verifies these exist before launching a browser. Captured in the extension's OWN light theme (--class vtt-light puts the shipped vtt-light class on <html>) — NOT the legacy screenshots/light-theme.capture.css override, which predates the product having a light theme. Capture from a capture build (`npm run build:capture`: production backends, no analytics): a dev build paints a lime 'backend: env' switch across the top of the panel.

files: promo-1..5.png (1280x800, upload to CWS) + @2x (2560x1600, for the website)

knownIssues: promo-3.png is NOT this pipeline's own render: it is out/fullscreen@1/fullscreen-guess.png, the same guess-mode message shot as a fullscreen frame rather than a panel crop (chosen 2026-08-27; the displaced panel-crop original is in archive/2026-08-27-v5-slide3-panelcrop/). UNLIKE v5, render.mjs now performs that substitution itself at the end of a run and fails the run if fullscreen-guess.png is missing — in v5 it was a manual `cp` recorded here, i.e. a step that silently ships the wrong picture the first time someone forgets it.

promo-5.png is NOT this pipeline's own render either: like slide 3, it is a fullscreen@1 frame (fullscreen-word.png), and render.mjs substitutes it at the end of a run. The panel-crop slide5.html that used to produce it was dropped — a short dictionary entry left the sidebar's lower half empty, so a cropped device read as a chopped-off panel and a whole one read as half-loaded. The fullscreen form has no such problem: the panel runs the full height of the frame by construction, and the slide matches the shape slides 1 and 3 already use. Its panel is a REPLICA (see fullscreen@1's own knownIssues) built from computed styles measured off the running extension in the DARK theme.

The captures must come from a build that carries the dictionary gateway (EXT_API_BASE_URL). The lookup card and the word screen are filled by a live LOOKUP_WORD round-trip, so a build without it answers 'lookup not configured' and both states silently never open — capture-backdrop.mjs warns ('never settled') but still writes a PNG.
history: 2026-09-18: forked from store-en@5 for the word lookup shipped in 1.0.21. Three changes. Slide 1 gained the hover card over its captions. Slide 2 was re-shot and stopped drawing product UI: v5 painted a '+ Lingogram' quick-add pill and a selection swatch in CSS, and BOTH controls had since been removed from the product (the '✓ saved' badge was deleted outright in a72f6c6, its message key dropped from all 57 locale files; the pill was replaced by the lookup card). The new capture carries the real evidence instead — words the learner owns wear the standing saved mark, which demo mode now produces by seeding the word mirror rather than by adding a promo-only class. Slide 5 is new: the word screen, as a fullscreen frame in the dark theme, taking the series to the store's five-per-locale cap.

2026-08-27: the fullscreen hero took slide 1, and the two slides it made redundant were dropped — the old opener ("Dual subtitles turn any video into a language lesson") and the old fullscreen slide ("Works on any video with subtitles"), whose claim the hero now carries. Both renders are kept under archive/2026-08-27-displaced-by-fullscreen-hero/. The series went 5 → 6 → 4; four is under the store's five-per-locale cap, so nothing has to be chosen at upload time.

2026-08-27: slide 2 was retargeted from dual subtitles to the personal dictionary ("Every word you save, in your own dictionary"). The saving mechanic was already present in the capture — demo mode marks a word via the same markSpansSaved() the real save flow uses — but at slide scale the 10px badge was invisible, so the slide read as another subtitle-list shot. assets/save-slide.css fixes that without faking any UI: a soft vertical dim over the panel so the saved card is what the eye lands on, plus a staged pre-save moment on "vamos" (selection swatch + quick-add pill). The body copy names the button and the destination — "tap + Lingogram ... straight to your personal dictionary on lingogram.ai" — matching the site's own wording (en.json feat4P/faq.words). An earlier draft also carried a word→pill→badge strip under the paragraph; it was dropped once the copy named the button, because it put a third + Lingogram on a slide that already showed two and retold the story the panel tells.

2026-08-27: slide 4 was retargeted from onboarding ("Set up once, then just press play" / FREE · NO ACCOUNT TO START) to customisation ("Every subtitle, tuned to your taste" / MAKE IT YOURS). The capture was always the settings panel; the copy just wasn't about it, and led on setup while naming only "size, colour and position". The new copy is specific and checked against SidebarUI.ts: FONT_OPTIONS holds 7 fonts, every swatch row ends in a custom colour well (<input type=color>) so "any colour" is literal rather than the 5 presets, and the main and translation lines carry separate size/colour prefs (overlayFontSize/overlayColor vs overlaySubFontSize/overlaySubColor, defaulting to 100%/#ffffff and 75%/#ffd700 — which is what the panel shows). The headline was then softened from "Every subtitle, tuned to your taste", which read as ad copy rather than as a description, to "Make the subtitles look how you want". A second panel — the same settings screen captured in the dark theme, offset behind the light one — was built and then REMOVED by decision on the same day. It worked visually, but the series already carries the dark theme on slides 1 and 3 (both fullscreen frames render the panel with fullscreen@1's dark sheet; measured 52% and 30% dark pixels against slide 4's 4%), so this made slide 4 the second telling of something already said, while costing the one frame where the light panel is shown whole. The dark band also could not carry the point on its own: the Theme row that would explain it was clipped out of the exposed strip. live-demo-settings-dark-en.png is kept in out-live/ if it is ever wanted. The dropped "free, no account to start" claim is still carried by the store listing itself; it was never something this capture illustrated.
